run.notes: Second reference case, built from the Corlander & Vale report v1.0 (synthetic). Used to check that Phase 4 is not tuned to Veloran only.

sources.loaded_hourly_rate: Average salary $100,000 x 1.30 plus $23,600 overhead per person, divided by 1,920 working hours (C&V finance, FY2026)
sources.working_weeks_per_year: 52 weeks minus PTO and holidays (C&V handbook)

formulas.hours_saved_per_week: effect share x hours lost per week, rounded to whole hours
formulas.annual_time_savings: hours saved x working weeks x loaded hourly rate x adoption
formulas.annual_deal_margin: deals lost x recovery share x adoption x average deal value x contribution margin
formulas.year_one_cost: upfront cost + first year of ongoing cost
formulas.mix_of_fixes: largest saving + each other saving x (1 - overlap); never more than the cap share of hours lost
formulas.choice: highest first-year net benefit among eligible mixes that pay back within the limit

bottlenecks.name: Client documents chased and re-requested by hand
root_causes: Every team chases on its own

options.label: Option 1: AI follow-up assistant
options.name: AI follow-up assistant
options.how_it_solves: AI inside the email client drafts follow-up emails from each client thread and summarizes long threads; staff still send and track them
example_vendors: Microsoft 365 Copilot Business (if the firm runs Microsoft 365)

governance.note: Medium: reads client email that holds confidential data; needs the AI policy and consent language first
go_live_gates: Approve a one-page AI acceptable-use policy

options.evidence: Corlander & Vale reference report v1.0, Bottleneck 1, Option 1

options.label: Option 2: Client portal with automatic reminders
options.name: Client portal with automatic reminders

options.label: Option 3: Intake desk and document deadline
options.name: Intake desk and document deadline
options.how_it_solves: One intake desk sends one combined request list per client, logs receipts and chases on a fixed schedule; anything incomplete on the deadline is extended by rule

effort.note: Medium: clients must hear the deadline in their engagement letters, and partners must hold it

options.evidence: Corlander & Vale reference report v1.0, Bottleneck 1, Option 3

bottlenecks.name: Returns and workpapers waiting in review, with rework
bottlenecks.category_label: Work waiting in review, with rework
root_causes: Returns reach review before they are ready
Every return goes to a partner

options.label: Option 1: AI pre-review agent
options.name: AI pre-review agent
options.how_it_solves: An agent reconciles each prepared return with its source documents and the prior year, and flags differences and risky items before a person reviews

effort.note: Medium: integration and client consent work

governance.note: High: full returns and source documents go to a third-party AI; needs signed client consent and a vendor review
go_live_gates: Signed client consent for AI processing
Approve a one-page AI acceptable-use policy

risks_and_dependencies: The vendor may not support the firm's software version
A clean AI check can breed false comfort
options.evidence: Corlander & Vale reference report v1.0, Bottleneck 2, Option 1
options.status_reason: Not recommended now: full client files would go to a third-party AI, which needs signed client consent and a vendor review first.
other_reasons: Deferred: an AI pre-review works best on work that arrives complete through a tracked queue (current: no). The recommended Client portal with automatic reminders creates this; revisit after one season on the portal.

options.label: Option 2: Review queues in the portal
options.name: Review queues in the portal
options.how_it_solves: Every item carries a status, a named reviewer and a due date; reviewers see their queue and its age; review notes are logged per item
example_vendors: Same vendor as the client portal
options.cost_note: $0 extra once the client portal is approved
risks_and_dependencies: Depends on the client portal decision

options.label: Option 3: Tiered review and review-ready checklist
options.name: Tiered review and review-ready checklist
options.how_it_solves: Preparers clear a one-page checklist before review; work is tiered by complexity so trained seniors sign off the simplest third and partners review only the complex third; a monthly debrief fixes the most repeated notes

effort.note: Medium: senior reviewers must let go of simple work

risks_and_dependencies: Quality must hold under peer review
options.evidence: Corlander & Vale reference report v1.0, Bottleneck 2, Option 3

upfront_breakdown.calc: 8 reviewers to train x 16 h x $80 = $10,240

trace.hours_saved_per_week: 0.416 share x 180.3 h lost = 75 -> 75 h a week

recommendation.together_note: The checklist cuts second reviews at the source, tiering moves simple work off senior desks, and the queue shows everyone what is waiting.
recommendation.summary: We recommend Option 3 (Tiered review and review-ready checklist) and Option 2 (Review queues in the portal) together. The checklist cuts second reviews at the source, tiering moves simple work off senior desks, and the queue shows everyone what is waiting. Together they save an estimated 100 hours a week ($268,800 a year) for $39,600 in year one, a payback of 1.8 months.

program.summary: The 3 recommendations cost $319,900 in year one and save an estimated $981,120 a year, a combined payback of 3.9 months. From year two, ongoing costs are $230,660 a year and the net benefit is about $750,460 a year. At 70% adoption, the 365 gross hours become about 256 effective hours a week: 43% of the 598 hours lost to the bottlenecks in scope.
